\subsubsection{Monte Carlo}\label{sss:tia-mc}

Section~\ref{sss:tia-loop} settles the loop over five process corners. Corners carry no
mismatch, so they cannot bound the offset of a differential pair, nor confirm that the
\SI{22}{\pico\farad} feedback capacitor holds once the amplifier is not matched to
itself. This section reports a 200-sample Monte Carlo run of the transimpedance stage,
seed 12345, low-discrepancy sampling, varying process and mismatch together
(\texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}) at \SI{37}{\celsius}. Both gain taps are run,
$R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$ and \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}, into the cell of
Figure~\ref{fig:randles-cell} with $R_s = \SI{100}{\ohm}$,
$R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{1}{\mega\ohm}$, $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$ and
$C_f = \SI{22}{\pico\farad}$. Figures are schematic-level, without extracted parasitics.

Every $\sigma$ below is a process-and-mismatch figure and is not comparable with a
mismatch-only $\sigma$; the variation type and model section are named in every caption.
Skewed quantities are quoted as 1st and 99th percentiles with the worst sample rather
than mean $\pm\,3\sigma$.

\paragraph{Convergence.} 48 of 400 samples do not converge --- 27 at
\SI{35}{\kilo\ohm} and 21 at \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}, so the surviving populations are 173
and 179 and the two yields below are computed on comparable footings. In a failing
sample the output sits at $v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ and the loop gain is degenerate, ranging from
\SI{45}{\decibel} down through zero to \SI{-49}{\decibel}: the loop is not merely weak,
it has lost its sign in some draws. They are excluded from every statistic here, and no
yield quoted below includes them. The amplifier is not at fault --- on its own bench
(\texttt{UnityFeedbackTB}) all 400 samples are healthy, with loop gain
\SIrange{69.6}{86.1}{\decibel}. The failure is in the closed-loop DC solution with the
electrode attached and is under investigation.
Consequently every DC-sweep-derived result --- gain error, INL, total unadjusted error,
signal bandwidth and the source-limit fraction --- is withheld from this revision, as it
degrades on the same samples.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Phase margin passes at both taps, \SI{100}{\percent}.} At
\SI{35}{\kilo\ohm} the mean is \SI{96.9}{\degree}, $\sigma = \SI{6.3}{\degree}$, worst
\SI{84.2}{\degree} (Table~\ref{tab:tia-mc-stab35k}). At \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm} the mean is
\SI{66.7}{\degree}, $\sigma = \SI{11.3}{\degree}$, worst \SI{46.6}{\degree} against the
\SI{45}{\degree} floor (Table~\ref{tab:tia-mc-stab560k},
Figure~\ref{fig:tia-mc-pm560k}). This is the result the corner run could not deliver:
its \SIrange{61.2}{64.9}{\degree} spread carries no mismatch. The
\SI{22}{\pico\farad} capacitor is validated, with \SI{1.6}{\degree} of margin at the
high-gain tap across 179 converged samples.

\item \textbf{Peaking is the softer failure.} At \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm} the mean is
\SI{1.15}{\decibel}, $\sigma = \SI{0.62}{\decibel}$, worst \SI{2.61}{\decibel} against a
\SI{2}{\decibel} criterion --- \SI{87.7}{\percent} of channels, and \SI{59.2}{\percent}
of four-channel parts. At \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm} peaking is identically \SI{0}{\decibel} on
every sample: the response there is monotonic, so the peak coincides with the
\SI{1}{\hertz} reference and the ratio is exactly one. That is a real absence of peaking,
not a clipped reading. The samples that exceed \SI{2}{\decibel} still hold their phase
margin, so this is a response-shape criterion failing before stability does.

\item \textbf{Loop gain has a tail that the mean hides.} DC loop gain averages
\SI{78.4}{\decibel} at \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm} and \SI{74.8}{\decibel} at
\SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}, but the worst converged samples reach \SI{22.6}{\decibel} and
\SI{-8.95}{\decibel} respectively, missing the \SI{60}{\decibel} criterion on
\SI{1.2}{\percent} and \SI{4.5}{\percent} of channels. A negative loop gain on a sample
whose transimpedance is otherwise correct is not physical, so this tail is most likely
the same degenerate-bias population as the excluded samples, caught by a convergence
filter that keys on transimpedance alone. Read the loop-gain row as an upper bound on
the failure rate until that is settled.

\item \textbf{Input offset is the binding problem.} $\sigma(v_{\mathrm{off}})$ is
\SI{4.70}{\milli\volt} at \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm} and \SI{7.09}{\milli\volt} at
\SI{560}{\kilo\ohm} against a \(\pm\SI{5}{\milli\volt}\) budget:
\SI{74.0}{\percent} and \SI{54.7}{\percent} of channels
(Table~\ref{tab:tia-mc-offset}, Figure~\ref{fig:tia-mc-voff}). Four identical channels
make chip yield approximately $p^4$, about \SI{9}{\percent} at the high-gain tap. This
is the failure shape the control amplifier already shows
(\(\sigma = \SI{4.82}{\milli\volt}\) against \SI{2}{\milli\volt},
Section~\ref{ss:controlamp}), and it is a mismatch quantity that no corner run can
bound. Trimming or chopping is required in both stages.

\item \textbf{Noise passes with margin.} Input-referred current noise over
\SIrange{0.1}{100}{\hertz} averages \SI{530}{\pico\ampere} at \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm} and
\SI{260}{\pico\ampere} at \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}. The worst sample reaches
\SI{1276}{\pico\ampere} against the \SI{2}{\nano\ampere} limit, so yield is
\SI{100}{\percent} at both taps with a factor of \num{1.6} in hand.
\end{enumerate}

Stability is therefore closed and accuracy is not. The open item for
Section~\ref{ss:tiaamp} is offset cancellation; the open item for this bench is the
non-convergent \SI{12}{\percent}.
